newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Nestle S.Africa strike drags on.
newsitem.headline: Nestle S.Africa strike drags on.

text.p: A strike for higher pay by about 2,800 workers at 10 South African factories of food and beverage group Nestle SA went into a fifth day on Monday with the company predicting no immediate resolution to it.
Nestle spokesman Humphrey Khoza said the company was scheduled to meet with the Food and Allied Workers Union (FAWU) on Tuesday over the wage impasse, but a speedy resolution was unlikely.
"There has been no change in the situation. There will be a meeting between FAWU and managment on Tuesday, (but)...a resolution in the very short term is unlikely," Khoza told Reuters

FAWU is demanding a 9.1 percent increase across the board plus a reduction of the 45-hour working week to 40 hours and the subsidising of workers for company supplies such as milk formulae for staff with young babies. The company has offered a nine percent wage increase.
Nestle employs 6,000 workers nationally and those not striking were continuing with their normal duty, Khoza said, adding he could not say how much in value terms the strike had cost the company.
"We are not able at this stage to estimate how much the company has lost and the overall impact that it (strike) has on the company," he said
FAWU officials were not available for comment.
